properties.areaDesc: Inland Volusia; Coastal Volusia
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 4:52PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
At 452 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm over
Edgewater, moving northeast at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Port Orange, New Smyrna Beach, Edgewater, South Daytona, and Daytona
Beach Shores.
properties.instruction:
If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

Conditions are favorable for the development of weak, brief funnel
clouds. On rare occasions they can briefly touch down, producing wind
gusts over 50 mph. If a funnel cloud is spotted move indoors and
report your sighting to the National Weather Service.

NWSheadline: A STRONG THUNDERSTORM WILL IMPACT EAST CENTRAL VOLUSIA COUNTY THROUGH 530 PM EDT

properties.areaDesc: Barnwell, SC
properties.headline: Tornado Warning issued October 10 at 4:52PM EDT until October 10 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
At 452 PM EDT, a confirmed tornado was located near Barnwell, moving
north at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Damaging tornado.

SOURCE...Radar confirmed tornado.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows, and vehicles will occur.  Tree damage is
likely.

Locations impacted include...
Kline.
properties.instruction:
To repeat, a tornado is on the ground. TAKE COVER NOW! If you are
outdoors, in a mobile home, or in a vehicle, move to an interior room
or closet on the lowest floor of a sturdy building immediately.

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 13 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...DAMAGING sea-water coastal flooding is likely through
Sunday, especially near the Sunday morning high tide where
anticipated tide levels are expected to be around 8 feet. The
most likely areas for DAMAGING coastal flooding on Sunday
morning will be vulnerable southeast facing beaches, such as
Avalon and Pebbly Beach. For all other beaches and harbors,
minor to moderate coastal flooding is expected. The most
DAMAGING and WIDESPREAD coastal flooding risk along southeast
beaches will likely be with the Sunday morning high tide due to
the expected combination of very high level tide levels
approaching 8 feet (including additive effect of low barometric
pressure, high surf of 5 to 8 feet, and light to moderate
rainfall.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM Sunday to 2 PM PDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Sea-water flooding of beach and harbor roads, parking
lots, and walkways is likely, especially around the time of high
tide. Isolated damage is likely across southeast facing beaches
near Sunday mornings high tide. Significant beach erosion is
expected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 8 feet are expected on
Sunday morning, returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and
Tuesday mornings. Large secondary high tides are also expected
each evening.
properties.instruction:
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 11 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...DAMAGING sea-water coastal flooding is likely through
Sunday, especially near the Sunday morning high tide where
anticipated tide levels are expected to be around 8 feet. The
most likely areas for DAMAGING coastal flooding on Sunday
morning will be vulnerable south-facing beaches due to the
expected combination of very high level tide levels around 8
feet (including additive effect of low barometric pressure and
onshore winds gusting to 15 to 25 mph), high surf of 5 to 8
feet, and light to moderate rainfall. For all other beaches,
minor to moderate coastal flooding is expected near times of
high tide. From Sunday night through Tuesday, there will be the
continued threat of at least minor to moderate coastal flooding
and elevated surf across Los Angeles county beaches, especially
south facing shores. Dangerous rip currents are likely.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM to 10 PM PDT Sunday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM Sunday to 2 PM PDT
Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...For vulnerable south-facing beaches (such as Alamitos
Peninsula and Naples in Long Beach as well as Malibu),
SIGNIFICANT sea- water flooding will likely DAMAGE coastal
structures and beach roadways around the time of high tide,
especially the Sunday morning high tide. In addition,
significant ponding of water on low-lying beach roadways could
make driving difficult. THERE IS GROWING CONFIDENCE THAT THE
EXPECTED COASTAL FLOODING IMPACTS ON SUNDAY MORNING FOR
VULNERABLE SOUTH FACING BEACHES OF LA COUNTY COULD BE THE MOST
SIGNIFICANT WE HAVE SEEN SO FAR THIS SEASON, INCLUDING THOSE
SEEN WITH MARIE. For all other beaches and harbors, shallow with
minor to moderate sea- water flooding will likely impact
beaches and walkways, especially with the Sunday morning high
tide which could cause local damage to most vulnerable locations
such as Venice. For all beach areas, significant erosion is
expected. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning.
Dangerous and life- threatening rip currents can pull swimmers
and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury,
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near
shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides of around 8 feet are expected on
Sunday morning (nearly 2 feet above astronomical high tide of
6.1 feet), returning to around 7.5 feet for Monday and Tuesday
mornings. The projected high tides of around 8 feet for Sunday
morning would approach or exceed recent record tide levels for
LA county. Large secondary high tides are also expected each
evening.
properties.instruction:
Follow directions of emergency officials.
Stay off of beaches and coastal walkways, roads, and structures.
Do NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 1:51PM PDT until October 12 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, Minor tidal overflow
flooding and strong rip currents are expected. For the Coastal
Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding can be
expected near times of high tide, especially with the Sunday
morning high tide. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 12 feet is expected with dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through late tonight.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 10 PM PDT
Monday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to 10 PM
PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at beach and harbor areas that is uncommon with
normal tidal ranges. Low lying areas will be most susceptible,
including Oceano. Enhanced beach erosion is likely. The risk for
significant damage is very low. There is an increased risk of
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Waves can wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats nearshore. Large secondary high tides are also
expected each evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around 7.5
feet on Sunday morning, then around 7 feet on Monday morning.

* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, minor tidal overflow
flooding with elevated surf and dangerous rip currents are
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding can be expected near times of high tide,
especially with the Sunday morning high tide.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Tuesday
afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM Sunday to
10 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
around high tide at low-lying beach and harbor areas that is
uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach erosion is
possible. The risk for significant damage is very low. There is
an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore. Large
secondary high tides are also expected each evening.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides are expected to peak around 7.7
feet on Sunday morning, then 7.1 to 7.3 feet on Monday and
Tuesday mornings.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 10 at 1:43PM PDT until October 12 at 2:00PM PDT by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...A moderate risk for sneaker waves is expected. Short
period north-northwest wind waves will interact with a
building west-northwest long period swell.

* WHERE...The beaches of Douglas, Coos, and Curry counties.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Monday afternoon. The
risk will be highest during Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Sneaker waves can run up significantly farther on
beaches than normal, including over rocks and jetties. These
waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and sweep
them into the ocean. The waves can also move logs or other
objects which could crush or trap anyone caught underneath.

* View the hazard area in detail at
https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:

remain out of the water to avoid hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Dust Advisory issued October 10 at 1:43PM MST until October 10 at 2:45PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Dust Advisory for...
Maricopa County in south central Arizona...
Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 245 PM MST.

* At 143 PM MST, a wall of dust was located along a line from over
Sun Lakes to 12 miles southwest of Casa Grande, moving east at 15
mph.

HAZARD...Less than one mile visibility with strong winds in excess
of 30 mph.

SOURCE...Public reported.

IMPACT...Hazardous travel.

* Locations impacted include...
Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Casa Grande, Coolidge, Sun Lakes, Queen
Creek, Arizona City, Olberg, Blackwater, San Tan Mountain Park,
Bapchule, Chandler Heights, Seville, Arizola, San Tan Valley,
Tumbleweed Park, San Tan Village Mall and Phoenix Mesa Gateway
Airport.

This includes the following highways...
AZ Route 87 between mile markers 135 and 144. AZ Interstate 8 between
mile markers 160 and 169. AZ Route 202 between mile markers 34 and
43. AZ Route 101 near mile marker 61. AZ Route 287 between mile
markers 111 and 120. AZ Interstate 10 between mile markers 163 and
172. AZ Route 347 near mile marker 189.
properties.instruction:
Blowing dust brings reduced visibility, leading to dangerous driving
conditions. If driving, avoid blowing dust if possible. If caught in
dense blowing dust, pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep
your foot off the brake.

To report hazardous dust conditions, contact the National Weather
Service, or your nearest law enforcement agency, who will relay your
report to the National Weather Service office in Phoenix AZ.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 10 at 1:38PM PDT until October 11 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning through Sunday afternoon,
significant coastal flooding and erosion is likely. For the
Beach Hazards Statement from Sunday morning until Sunday
evening, surf of 5 to 7 feet with local sets up to 9 feet. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory from Sunday afternoon until Tuesday
afternoon, minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 3 PM PDT Sunday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning through
Sunday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 PM
Sunday to 2 PM PDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads and walking paths may be closed due
to high water. Low-lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may flood. Shoreline erosion
will occur during high tides in the mornings. Elevated surf
will lead to a high risk of rip currents.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Greatest impacts on Sunday morning from
Tropical Storm Rachel with a combination of increased swell,
onshore winds, and high tides locally over 7.5 feet. High tides
lower each day into the middle of the week.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 4:36PM EDT until October 10 at 6:30PM EDT by NWS Columbia SC
properties.description:
FFWCAE

The National Weather Service in Columbia has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Burke County in east central Georgia...
Southeastern Columbia County in east central Georgia...
Richmond County in east central Georgia...
West Central Aiken County in central South Carolina...
South Central Edgefield County in central South Carolina...

* Until 630 PM EDT.

* At 436 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
North Augusta, Grovetown, Evans, Fort Gordon, Augusta, Martinez,
Clearwater, Belvedere, Hephzibah, South Augusta, Augusta Regional
Airport, Augusta Mall, Glendale, Daniel Field, Summerville,
Midtown, McBean, Village Plaza Shopping Center, Augusta National
Golf Club and Gloverville.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 520 in South Carolina between mile markers 16 and 23.
Interstate 20 in South Carolina between mile markers 0 and 7.
Interstate 20 in Georgia between mile markers 192 and 201. Interstate
520 in Georgia between mile markers 1 and 15.
properties.instruction:
Most flooding deaths occur in vehicles. Never drive through a flooded
roadway or around barricades. Turn around, don't drown.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 4:02PM EDT until October 11 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...In Northeast Georgia, the following counties: Elbert,
Franklin, Habersham, Hart, Rabun and Stephens. In western North
Carolina, the following counties: Avery, Buncombe, Burke, Caldwell,
McDowell, Polk,  Rutherford, Haywood, Henderson, Macon, Mitchell,
Jackson, Transylvania and Yancey. In Upstate South Carolina, the
following counties: Abbeville, Anderson, Central Greenville,
Greater Oconee, Greater Pickens, Greenville, Greenwood, Laurens,
Spartanburg, and Oconee.

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings
may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- As Isaias weakens and moves northward into the lower Ohio Valley,
periods of rain will continue. While rainfall rates may decrease
in some areas this evening, short bursts of heavy rain are
possible through tonight. By Sunday morning, total accumulations
of generally 5 to 8 inches are expected along the
southeast-facing Blue Ridge Escarpment, with 2 to 5 inches
elsewhere in the watch area.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Watch for flash flooding means there is a potential for rapid
onset flooding based on current forecasts. Flash flooding is a very
dangerous situation and may impact areas that do not typically flood.
Please monitor the latest forecasts and be prepared to take action
quickly should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Rainfall of more than five inches in similar storms has been
associated with an increased risk of landslides, especially
fast-moving debris flows and debris slides. If you live on a
mountainside or in a cove at the base of a mountain, especially near
a stream, be ready to leave in advance of the storm and follow
evacuation orders from local officials. Consider postponing travel
along mountain roads during the heavy rainfall event.

properties.description:
* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 002 Ontonagon and Fire
Weather Zone 009 Gogebic.

* TIMING...Until 6 PM EDT /5 PM CDT/ Sunday.

* WINDS...South 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph...diminishing
to 10 to 15 mph with gusts to 25 mph late tonight into Sunday.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 31 percent this
afternoon...recovering to 60 to 70 percent tonight. Sunday, as
low as 30 to 40 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of
strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures and
exceptionally dry fuels will create dangerous wildland fire
conditions. Campfires, outdoor grills, smoking materials,
fireworks, chain saws, and all-terrain vehicles all have the
potential to throw a spark and ignite a dangerous and destructive
fire.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 10 at 8:31AM SST by NWS Pago Pago  AS
properties.description:
ESFPPG

An active trough to the north is projected to drift southward and
move over the territory by Tuesday of next week. This trough is
likely to remain strong and active through the duration of next
week, and may even intensify with embedded low pressure centers.
Widespread showers may be heavy and persistent at times with the
possibility of thunderstorms Tuesday through the weekend.
Widespread flash flooding may occur from this rainfall. Landslides
will be possible along steep mountainous terrain. While there is
still uncertainty in the exact magnitude and duration of rainfall,
plan now for wet conditions next Tuesday through at least Sunday.

Keep up to date with the latest forecast information through our
internet page (www.weather.gov/ppg), local media, social media,
and our NOAA Radio broadcasts.

NWSheadline: Flash Flooding and landslide potential for Tuesday through Sunday of next week

expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

and Eastern Essex Counties.

* WHEN...From 11 AM to 6 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Shallow flooding is expected in the most vulnerable
locations near the waterfront and shoreline resulting in a low
threat of property damage. Expect up to one foot of water
above ground level in low lying, vulnerable areas. Some roads
and low lying property including parking lots, parks and lawns
near the waterfront will experience shallow flooding.
properties.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 3:04PM EDT until October 11 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast North Carolina, including the
following areas, Coastal Brunswick, Coastal New Hanover, Coastal
Pender, Columbus, Inland Brunswick, Inland New Hanover and Inland
Pender and northeast South Carolina, including the following areas,
Central Horry, Coastal Georgetown, Coastal Horry, Inland Georgetown
and Northern Horry.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Tropical moisture continues to overspread the area tonight
through Sunday with showers and thunderstorms producing heavy
rainfall at times. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches
are expected with the highest totals likely in the Cape Fear
area. A few areas could receive up to 6 inches in thunderstorms,
mainly tonight. This excessive rainfall could lead to flooding,
especially in flood prone and low-lying areas.
- weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 10 at 3:00PM EDT until October 12 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
Moderate to heavy rainfall is expected as the remnants of Isaias
track across the region starting early Sunday morning. Storms should
be highly efficient rainfall producers given the tropical nature of
the air mass. In particular, the eastern slopes of the Blue Ridge
have the potential to see the most rainfall given the continued
easterly upslope winds. A further eastward expansion of these watches
may be needed.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Portions of central, northern, and northwest Virginia,
including the following areas, in central Virginia, Albemarle,
Central Virginia Blue Ridge, Greene, Nelson and Orange. In northern
Virginia, Culpeper, Northern Fauquier and Southern Fauquier. In
northwest Virginia, Madison, Northern Virginia Blue Ridge and
Rappahannock.

* WHEN...From late tonight through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The remnants of Isaias will bring a tropical air mass much into
the Mid-Atlantic region late tonight into Sunday. Storms should
be highly efficient in this environment and capable of producing
several inches of rain throughout the duration of the event.
Storm total rainfall is expected to be around 2 to 3 inches, with
pockets of 3 to 5 inches along the eastern slopes of the Blue
Ridge.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3
to 7 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to
one foot of inundation above ground level expected in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Pender and Coastal New Hanover Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 AM EDT Sunday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, until 8 PM EDT this evening. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 PM to 11 PM EDT this
evening.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 2:14PM EDT until October 11 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Kent.

* WHEN...From 7 AM to 1 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most vulnerable
roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along inland tidal
waterways. Some partial or full road closures are possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...western Coconino, northern Gila, far southern Navajo, and
Yavapai counties.

* WHEN...Through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms are expected to increase in coverage
through today, and continue through the overnight hours into
Sunday. With deep tropical moisture in place from the remnants of
Tropical Storm Rachel, periods of embedded heavy rainfall will be
possible leading to flash flooding. Additionally, the extended
period of rain could lead to elevated flow in creeks, normally
dry washes, and rivers.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:

action should warnings be issued.

properties.areaDesc: Cleveland, NC; Cherokee, SC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 2:03PM EDT until October 13 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory is extended for the following rivers in South
Carolina...North Carolina...

(English) Broad River Near at Shelby Hwy (SC 18), 4 W Blacksburg
affecting Cleveland and Cherokee Counties.

.Heavy tropical showers will continue to overspread the Broad River
basin through tonight with 3 or 4 inches of rain accumulating.
Excessive runoff remains likely to develop pushing the river out of
it's banks on Sunday.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...(English) Broad River near at Shelby Hwy (SC 18), 4 W
Blacksburg.

* WHEN...Until Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues. At this
level, minor flooding of low-lying farmland along the river may be
ongoing. Areas along Buffalo Breek may be beginning to flood due to
backwater effects. At 15.0 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues.
The Broad River may be approaching River Rd. and Little Hope Rd.
near US 29.  Adjacent farmland and low-lying area flooding is
continuing.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.7 feet and rising slowly.
- Bankfull stage is 13.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.9 feet
Monday morning with a reasonable worse case scenario of near 18
feet.
- Action stage is 13.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

For detailed information including observed and forecast stages,
flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,
please visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP

The next statement should be issued late tonight before 215 AM EDT.

...The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued
a Flood Warning for the following rivers in North Carolina...

(English) Broad River At above Sandy Run Ck, 3 SSW Boiling Springs
affecting Cleveland County.

.Heavy tropical showers will continue to overspread the Broad River
basin through tonight with 3 to 4 inches accumulating with locally as
much as 8 inches possible in favored locales and higher elevations.
Confidence has increased that flooding along the Broad River will
develop this weekend.  Interests all along the Broad River, even as
far upstream as Bat Cave are urged to monitor river levels and take
appropriate action as needed.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...(English) Broad River at above Sandy Run Ck, 3 SSW Boiling
Springs.

* WHEN...From Sunday night to Monday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.5 feet and rising.  A
crest exceeding 12.0 feet is likely to occur on Sunday with the
river reaching 14.0 a probable worst case scenario.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Monday morning to a crest of 13.2 feet Monday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage late Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 13.2
feet on 09/26/1929.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued October 10 at 9:31AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...The Imperial County APCD has issued an air quality alert
due to harmful levels of particle pollution from windblown dust.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...the Imperial Valley. Levels of particle pollution can vary
by time and location depending on emissions and local weather
conditions.

* WHEN...Sunday, October 11, 2026 from 12:00 AM until 10:00 PM.

* IMPACTS... Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and
cause serious health problems such as asthma attacks, heart and lung
disease symptoms, and increased risk of lung infections. Everyone
can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with lung or
heart disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment

To help minimize outdoor particle pollution levels:

* Carpool, telecommute, reduce trips, or take public
transportation
* Slow down if driving on dirt roads
* Stabilize loose soils
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 11:29AM EDT until October 12 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River Near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher
affecting Henderson and Buncombe Counties.

.Tropical rain showers will continue to overspread the mountains
through tonight becoming increasingly heavy, leading to excessive
runoff and rises on streams within the upper French Broad River
watershed.  Storm-total rainfall of 4-8 inches is expected, with
isolated 8-10 inches possible within the upper French Broad River
watershed, generally upstream of Etowah.  The highest totals will
occur along the Tanassee and Pisgah ridges, with lesser amounts
within the upper French Broad River valley.  Additionally, 4-6 inches
of rainfall are expected within the Mud Creek watershed in Henderson
County, which is a primary tributary of the French Broad River above
Fletcher.  While there continues to be some uncertainty regarding the
exact location, timing, and amounts of the heaviest rainfall, there
is enough confidence in the current forecast that out-of-bank
conditions are likely for the upper French Broad River. This rise
above Action Stage will result in nuisance, relatively shallow
flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to the French Broad River,
including farmland, woodlands, low-lying secondary roads, greenways,
parks, and other flood-prone locations.

More significant rises along the French Broad River are possible, and
those with interests along the river are encouraged to stay weather
aware and up-to-date on the latest stream levels and forecasts at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP.  Current reasonable worst-case
scenarios are posted in the ADDITIONAL DETAILS sections below.
Forecast crests above Minor Flood Stage may result in the River Flood
Advisories being upgraded to River Flood Warnings.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage.  The French Broad
River has exceeded bankfull at the gauge site.  Isolated farmland
flooding is beginning across the French Broad River Valley from
Etowah downstream to Avery Creek upstream of the gauge site.

* At 11.5 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues.  Butler Bridge Rd.
is inundated with up to 6 inches of floodwaters from the French
Broad River, forcing road closure.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.8 feet and rising.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.6 feet
early tomorrow afternoon.  A crest closer to 12 feet is possible.
A reasonable worst-case crest above Minor Flood Stage below 15
feet cannot be ruled out.
- Action stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

For detailed information including observed and forecast stages,
flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,
please visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP

The next statement should be issued this evening before 1130 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; San Diego County Inland Valleys; San Diego County Mountains; San Diego County Deserts
properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 10 at 8:07AM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
HLSSGX

This product covers EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA

**Impacts from Tropical Storm Rachel Expected in San Diego County Late
Tonight through Sunday Afternoon**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for San Diego County
Coastal Areas, San Diego County Deserts, San Diego County
Mountains, and San Diego County Valleys

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 560 miles south-southwest of San Mateo Point CA or about
510 miles south-southwest of Mouth of Tijuana River CA
- 25.5N 119.6W
- Storm Intensity 60 mph
- Movement Northeast or 55 degrees at 22 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Rachel is currently about 520 miles south-southwest of
San Diego, moving northeast towards Northern Baja at about 22 mph.
Rachel is expected to make landfall somewhere just south of the
US/Mexico Border Saturday evening. Tropical storm level impacts will
likely affect San Diego County. A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for
all of San Diego County. The main concerns with Tropical Storm Rachel
are coastal flooding, wind, and periods of heavy rain which could lead
to localized flooding and flash flooding. The majority of impacts from
the tropical storm are expected late tonight through early Sunday
afternoon.

South swell from Tropical Storm Rachel will arrive on Sunday. The
combination of south and northwest swells, increased onshore winds,
and high tides over 7 feet will maintain a threat of coastal flooding
and beach erosion along area beaches. Surf on Sunday is currently
expected to peak at 6 to 9 feet, decreasing to 3 to 6 feet for Monday
and Tuesday. Confidence in impactful coastal flooding is high, with
significant coastal flooding and beach erosion likely.

Widespread rain is expected on Sunday from Tropical Storm Rachel.
There is expected to be a gradient in rainfall amounts with the higher
amounts on the southeastern side of the storm. Confidence is high that
the heaviest rain will occur over San Diego County mountains and
deserts. Peak rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.60 inches are possible for
the coast and valleys, 0.50 to 0.70 inches per hour possible for the
deserts, and 0.70 to 1 inch per hour for the mountains. Current
forecast has rainfall totals of 0.50 to 1.25 inches for the coast,
valleys, and deserts and 1 to 2.5 inches for the mountains. Areas of
flash and urban flooding are probable, especially where the maximum
rainfall rates occur. The San Diego River at Fashion Valley is
currently forecast to peak at 7.4 feet (just below monitor stage)
Sunday afternoon. Those with interests near the San Diego River should
continue to monitor the forecast.

Increased winds are expected with the onset and passage of Tropical
Storm Rachel. Sustained winds of 39+ mph are expected on the southeast
side of the storm. Based on the current track, more southern and
eastern parts of San Diego County are most likely to see winds of this
magnitude. Regardless, strong sustained winds and wind gusts can be
expected on Sunday. Winds will likely be enhanced by local terrain
with gusts 40 to 55 mph on the desert slopes of the mountains and into
the deserts. Local gusts up to 60 mph possible on mountain ridges and
in passes and canyons. Winds are expected to remain elevated in
Rachel's wake with continued strong gusts on the desert mountain
slopes into the deserts through Monday morning.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* COASTAL HAZARDS:
High tides over 7 ft, combined with high surf and gusty onshore winds
will increase the threat for coastal flooding across area beaches.
Additionally surf of 6 to 9 ft will create dangerous swimming
conditions. Significant coastal flooding and beach erosion is likely.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across San Diego County. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos, and
ditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,
destructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides. Flood
control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts across San Diego County.

* WIND:
Prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts across
EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA. Potential impacts in this area
include:
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees are
shallow rooted, especially in coastal and valley locations that
don't typically experience strong winds. Some fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within urban
or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving conditions on
bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

Elsewhere across EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA, little to no impact
is anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
near the ocean, in a low-lying or poor drainage area, in a valley, or
near a river, plan to move to safe shelter on higher ground.

Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued. Do not needlessly jeopardize your life or the lives of
others.

Closely monitor weather.gov, NOAA Weather Radio and local news
outlets for official storm information. Listen for possible changes
to the forecast.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in San Diego CA around 2 PM PDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

Impacts from Tropical Storm Rachel Expected in San Diego County Late
Tonight through Sunday Afternoon

Cypress Creek At SR 54 Worthington Gardens affecting Pasco County.

Anclote River At Elfers at Little Road affecting Pasco County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Citrus and Levy
Counties.

.Due to recent heavy rainfall, water levels on Cypress Creek and
Anclote River remain elevated. With additional heavy rainfall
forecast, water levels are expected to continue rising, and could
reach minor flood stage in the next few days.

Elevated water levels continue on the Withlacoochee River at
Dunnellon due to a combination of excessive hydrilla growth along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between U.S. 41 and Lake Rousseau, and
recent heavy rainfall. Water levels are expected to hold steady
before slowly decreasing over the next several days. However, the
river is forecast to remain in flood stage.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 28.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:45 AM EDT Saturday was 28.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 28.3 feet
this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.3
feet on 10/05/1965.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 6 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late tonight. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM to 5 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 10:57AM EDT until October 12 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

Pigeon River At above Old River Rd (NC 215), 1 SW Canton affecting
Haywood County.

.Tropical rainfall will continue to overspread the mountains through
tonight and become heavier. Storm-total rainfall of 4-8 inches is
expected, with isolated higher amounts possible across the upper
Pigeon River watershed upstream of Canton.  The highest totals will
occur along the Pisgah ridge and in the Shining Rock and Middle Prong
Wilderness areas within the headwaters of the east and west forks of
the Pigeon River.  There remains enough confidence that  out-of-bank
conditions are likely for the Pigeon River.  This rise above Action
Stage will result in nuisance, relatively shallow flooding of
low-lying areas adjacent to the Pigeon River, including farmland,
woodlands, low-lying secondary roads, greenways, parks, and other
flood-prone locations.

More significant rises along the Pigeon River are possible, and those
with interests along the river are encouraged to stay weather aware
and up-to-date on the latest stream levels and forecasts at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP.  Current reasonable worst-case
scenarios are posted in the ADDITIONAL DETAILS sections below.
Forecast crests above Minor Flood Stage may result in the River Flood
Advisories being upgraded to River Flood Warnings.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Pigeon River at above Old River Rd (NC 215), 1 SW Canton.

* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage.  Common, nuisance
flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to the Pigeon River is
beginning.  Floodwaters are beginning to impact farmland,
woodlands, nurseries, parks, athletic fields, golf courses,
greenways, and boat-access areas with up to 2 feet of inundation.
Low-water crossings may be inundated with up to 2 feet of
floodwater and become impassable.  Adjacent campgrounds, mobile
home/RV parks, and secondary roads may experience floodwater
inundation of up to 1 foot.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 1.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.5 feet
tomorrow morning.  The reasonable worst-case crest would be
around the minor flood stage of 10 feet.
- Action stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard and away from rocks, jetties, and piers. If
caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Pike
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 6:20AM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
A period of strong wind gusts is expected today as the remnants
of Hurricane Isaias move into eastern Kentucky. Southeasterly
winds of 10 to 20 mph, with gusts up to 35 mph are expected. The
strongest winds are expected during the afternoon and should
coincide with the arrival of the leading bands of rain. Once
rainfall becomes steady, many areas will see the winds lighten,
except at elevations above 1,500 feet, where the gusty winds are
expected to continue into the night. Isolated gusts over 40 mph
are possible over the highest ridge tops. The gusty winds could
blow around unsecured outdoor objects and decor.

NWSheadline: Gusty Winds Expected Today and Tonight with the Remnants of Hurricane Isaias

properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 10 at 6:15AM EDT until October 11 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts of 35 to 50 mph
expected over higher terrain above 1,500 feet and in the valleys
immediately northwest of the Pine, Black, Cumberland, and Log
Mountains. Communities at greatest risk for the strongest wind
gusts include Cumberland, Eolia, Chenoa, Frakes, and Mayking.
Locations further removed from these taller prominent mountains
should expect southeast winds of 10 to 15 mph with occasional gusts
of 20 to 35 mph.

* WHERE...Bell, Harlan, and Letcher Counties.

* WHEN...From noon today to 5 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs and weakly rooted trees in steep terrain could be blown down
and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Communities at greatest risk for the strongest
wind gusts include Cumberland, Eolia, Chenoa, Frakes, and Mayking.
Locations further removed from these taller prominent mountains
should expect southeast winds of 10 to 15 mph with occasional gusts
of 20 to 35 mph.
properties.instruction:

profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Castle
Country, Central Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, San
Rafael Swell, Sanpete Valley, Sevier Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book
Cliffs, Bryce Canyon Country, Capitol Reef National Park and
Vicinity, Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central
Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper Sevier River Valleys, Western
Canyonlands, Lower Washington County, Southwest Utah and Zion
National Park. This also includes recent burn scars such as
Forsyth, Cottonwood, Silver King, France Canyon, and Monroe Canyon.

* WHEN...From noon MDT today through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,

properties.areaDesc: Lincoln; Lyon; Murray; Cottonwood; Pipestone; Kingsbury; Brookings; Lake; Moody
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 2:46AM CDT by NWS Sioux Falls SD
properties.description:
South winds gusting as high as 40 to 45 mph will develop quickly
by mid to late morning. Wind speeds will ease across east-central
South Dakota by mid afternoon, while the stronger gusts linger in
southwest Minnesota through sunset.

These strong winds, combined with near-record warmth and humidity
levels as low as 25 to 35 percent, will produce elevated fire
weather concerns today. Grassland fire danger will reach the High
category, with locally higher fire danger in cured croplands and
grasses.

Avoid outdoor burning and use extra caution with equipment in dry
crops, as rapid fire spread is possible.

In addition to the elevated fire danger, winds gusting over 40 mph
may produce areas of blowing dust, locally reducing visibility and
air quality.

properties.areaDesc: Traverse; Big Stone; Marshall; Roberts; Day; Clark; Codington; Grant; Hamlin; Deuel
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 10 at 1:47AM CDT by NWS Aberdeen SD
properties.description:
Warm and dry conditions will combine with strong wind gusts today
to create elevated fire weather concerns over the area this
afternoon. Due to abnormal warmth, minimum afternoon humidity
will drop to 25 to 35 percent. Strong southerly winds are expected
this morning, gusting up to 25 to 35 miles per hour. Some
localized gusts up to 45 miles per hour will be possible. Winds
are expected to decrease through the afternoon, meaning that the
strongest winds will not coincide with the lowest afternoon
humidity. However, gusts up to 30 miles per hour may linger into
the afternoon. Grassland Fire Danger will reach the High Category
as a result of the wind and humidity combination. Additionally,
these strong winds may create blowing dust today, causing
visibility reductions at times.

* IMPACTS...Large, unexpected waves can sweep across the beach

properties.instruction:

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: San Francisco; Northern Monterey Bay; Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 9 at 3:16PM PDT until October 13 at 3:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.4 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, increased risk of rip currents and sneaker waves
expected with breaking waves up to 16 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern
Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 3 PM PDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Saturday morning through
Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical. Dangerous conditions are
forecast along the shoreline. Hazards include sneaker waves,
strong rip currents, and large breaking waves.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.4 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 11:50 AM
Saturday 10/10, 1.4 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:18 PM
Sunday 10/11, 1.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 12:46 PM
Monday 10/12, and 1.1 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 1:14 PM
Tuesday 10/13. These predictions include up to 1.2 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,

possible.

properties.description:
The following statement was issued by the Oklahoma Department of
Environmental Quality from 10 AM to 10 PM CDT Saturday.

An Air Quality Alert for Ozone has been issued for Saturday, October
10th, for the Lawton area due to expected high concentrations of
ozone.

Public Health Recommendations: Persons with existing heart or
respiratory ailments should reduce physical exertion and outdoor
activity.

The general public is encouraged to help alleviate the problem by
reducing vehicle miles traveled by riding the bus, carpooling, or
avoiding unnecessary trips. The public is also asked to avoid
refueling during the morning and early afternoon hours, and to avoid
the use of two cycle engines such as lawn mowers, motorcycles, weed
trimmers, and outboard engines. It is also advised to limit outdoor
burning.

To view the latest air quality map, visit airnow.gov or the AirNow
app.

For hourly updates on concentrations and possible health warnings,
telephone the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality at
405-702-4100. For more information on health effects, call the
American Lung Association of Oklahoma at 405-748-4674

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 9 at 10:53AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
ESFGJT

A strong low pressure system off the Pacific Coast will begin to draw
in tropical moisture associated with Topical Storm Rachel this
weekend. This strong southerly fetch will draw anomalously high
moisture content across the Desert Southwest and into eastern Utah
and western Colorado. The chance for widespread precipitation
increases Saturday evening into Sunday. Total precipitation forecasts
range from 1 to 3 inches across high terrain, with highest amounts
favoring the Uintas, Tavaputs and the Southwest San Juan mountains.

Embedded thunderstorms are also possible Sunday afternoon, increasing
the threat for flash flooding across vulnerable terrain. While
confidence in location and rainfall rates remain low at this time,
the potential for rapidly rising rivers, streams, normally dry
arroyos and slot canyons are possible Sunday through Monday.

Please follow the evolving forecast, especially if your plans
including recreating or commuting across eastern Utah and western
Colorado Sunday onward. Also, keep in mind weather potential above
your location and upstream, particularly for those who reside below
sensitive terrain like recent burn scars.
